doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

chapter: The Bay Area scene and tastes
title: Desert island records
summary: Records he has worn out: Monk, Ray Charles with Ralph Burns, Trane Ballads, Miles, Duke at Newport.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: If you were going to be stranded on a beach — where did you go to interview school — I don’t pull this question out often. I’ll just say do you have three or four recordings that just are —
Yeah. “Monk at the Five Spot” with Johnny Griffin. Ray Charles with I guess part of the record is Quincy Jones and part of the record is —
No, no. God. The arranger. I’m blanking here. The guy that wrote “Early Autumn.” Oh this is terrible.
Oh I know who you mean too and I can’t. Ralph?
Isn’t that awful. We’ll both think of it later. Ralph Burns.
Ralph Burns. That record. It’s a great record. You know that’s two, you want five right?

All right. “Trane Ballads” I love that record, that band, I got to hear that band here in San Francisco, Elvin and McCoy and Jimmy Garrison, Trane. And I’ve got to put some Miles in there, which one? Maybe “Milestones.” Is that the one with “Billy Boy?”
Yes it is and the tune called “Miles.” [scats]. I love that record.

No Miles’ tunes, I know that tune, the record I’m thinking of is the one with Trane and Philly Joe and they do trio stuff with Red Garland I guess, but they do “Salt Peanuts” I think and stuff like that. Anyway, any of that stuff. God it would be hard to pick one. Aw there’s so many, and Duke. “Duke at Newport” I guess would be the — but “Duke at Newport” is — I mean if you wanted, if someone says what is swing? What is swinging? Just put on “Duke at Newport.” Put on “Dimenuendo and Crescendo in Blue” with Paul Gonsalves and Sam Woodyard back there.
That’s swinging. And I don’t know maybe Sinatra “Only the Lonely” or something like that. Beautiful stuff. I mean there are just too many.
